title: Automating the boring parts
summary: How repetitive geotechnical work pushed a civil engineer toward Python, data and eventually AI.

body: I trained as a civil engineer at Universiti Putra Malaysia and started my career at G&P Geotechnic. The engineering was real. So was the pile of repetitive work around it: the same calculations, the same spreadsheets, the same reports.

So I taught myself Python and VBA and started automating the boring parts. That cut the manual effort on those workflows by about 30%, but the bigger change was in me: I realised I cared more about the data than the drawings.

items.title: Nights
items.detail: I studied for the Certified Data Analyst Associate, PCEP and Power BI certifications.

items.title: The switch
items.detail: I left engineering for a Data Analyst role at EISmartwork, building models on more than ten million records.

items.title: Going deeper
items.detail: I started a Master’s in AI at UMPSA while working, and finished with a CGPA of 3.76.

body: Looking back, nothing about the move was a clean break. Engineering taught me to respect systems. Automation taught me that the most useful software starts with somebody being annoyed by a spreadsheet.
